title: Airmen Climbers Prep for Emergency Rescue on Denali
description:
Air Force Lt. Col. Rob Marshall talks with a National Park Service rescue crew ahead of an emergency evacuation of a fellow mountaineer. A six-man team was hiking to the top of Denali, North America's tallest mountain, as part of the Seven Summits Challenge when the emergency unfolded. 

Video by Air Force Lt. Col. Rob Marshall

transcript.text: (Air Force Lt. Col. Rob Marshall) We are lucky people to live in a country where, at 19,000 feet, somebody can get a deadly illness…
[over radio] Rob Marshall with Air Force [inaudible] you got a copy on address, channel one.

[over radio] You're going to see us in the helicopter coming by, you probably see us right now. We'll be coming by in a minute to do a power check, recon check flight. After that point, we're going to fly away. And then we'll return, and we'll kind of walk you through that in a little bit.
[off camera] We are hunkered in. We are sheltered in place.

(Marshall) So, what they're doing now is that power check, like I was telling you guys. Like, 'Hey, the winds are calm. Do we have the juice to pick up?' Mark probably knows a little bit more. They want to know what's the density altitude; if the winds change, how much of an effect would a sudden tailwind happen.
